name: Viking 1
intro: Viking 1 was the first NASA spacecraft to land safely on Mars, on 20 July 1976. It took the first pictures from the surface and reported the weather for more than six years. It still stands on the plain of Chryse Planitia, silent since 1982.
whyLeft: It was never meant to come home. In November 1982 a software update by mistake erased the data it used to aim its antenna at Earth, and the team could never reach it again.
repurpose: Engineers learned to test updates carefully and keep backups, the same care that saved Voyager 1 in 2024. A helper robot landing nearby could check how 50 years on Mars changed its metal and paint.

hotspots.title: The dish to Earth
hotspots.text: This dish talked straight to Earth. In November 1982 a software update meant to help Viking 1’s tired batteries accidentally wiped out the numbers it used to aim this dish, and the team never heard from it again.

hotspots.title: Two cameras
hotspots.text: Viking 1’s cameras took the first picture ever made on the surface of Mars, just minutes after landing on 20 July 1976. The very first thing they photographed was the lander’s own footpad.

photo.alt: Grainy black-and-white strip of rocks and dust, with a round lander footpad at the right.
photo.caption: The first photo ever taken on the surface of Mars, on 20 July 1976. Viking 1’s own footpad sits in the dust at the right.

hotspots.title: The soil scoop
hotspots.text: This arm reached out to scoop up soil and fed it into small labs inside the lander that tested it for signs of life. The results were puzzling, and most scientists now think strange soil chemistry, not living things, caused them.

hotspots.title: Nuclear power
hotspots.text: Two small nuclear generators on top kept Viking 1 warm and charged its batteries. A scout would check them first: they still give off a little heat, but the lander’s 1970s electronics have sat in the freezing cold for more than 40 years.

funFact: In 1982 Viking 1 was renamed the Thomas Mutch Memorial Station, after the leader of the Viking camera team.
